Starting point
AI system and date: Gemini, Nov 6, 2026
Before using AI for the required extension, briefly state your question, course-based core model, baseline result, and the specific limitation or opportunity you wanted to address. Research Question: To what extent do nutritional components (total fat, saturated fat, trans fat, sodium, carbs, fiber, sugar, protein) and restaurant chain predict the cholesterol content in fast-food menu items?
Baseline Model: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) multiple linear regression predicting cholesterol from nutritional macronutrients and restaurant indicators.
Limitation of Baseline: Linear regression assumes additive, straight-line relationships between nutrients and cholesterol. It struggles to capture non-linear patterns and complex multi-way interactions (for instance, the joint effect of high sodium and saturated fat on cholesterol within fried items versus grilled items).

title: AI Use and Verification
text:
My decisions

Accepted: We will use a Random Forest Regressor as a non-parametric benchmark to capture non-linearities and multi-nutrient interactions that linear models struggle with.
Changed: We limited the predictors (total fat, saturated fat, trans fat, sodium, carbs, fiber, sugar, protein) and restaurant brand, rather than letting the AI include redundant items like total calories or item names.
Rejected or corrected: Rejected overly complex hyperparameter tuning suggestions

Connection to the final case study: The Random Forest methods will be integrated into the Model Comparison and Advanced Analysis section of our final report, It will serve as a useful comparison to an OLS model. ## Independent verification

Check and result: 5-Fold Cross-Validation Metric Comparison: We will evaluate both the baseline linear regression and the Random Forest model using the exact same 5-fold cross-validation splits.
Check and result: We will plot predicted values versus residuals for the Random Forest to ensure residuals are randomly distributed around zero and do not display systematic bias.

title: Cholesterol in Fast Food
text:
The question
Can we predict cholesterol accurately from other nutritional information and the restaurant a food comes from? Which nutrients are the most influential? Answering these questions will inform consumers of fast food and spread awareness on fast food health. Our response variable is cholesterol (mg), and some of the important candidate predictors include company, calories, total fat, saturated fat, sodium, carbs, fibers, sugars, and proteins.
